title: Memory-driven price rises and AI shopping both reshape how we sell online
summary: Dell sees memory supply tight into 2027; PCB shortage lasts to mid-2028; European notebook revenue +16% on pricier models (DigiTimes). Half of holiday shoppers plan AI use (NRF); Walmart joined Meta's Muse agent.

points.headline: Memory and component shortages will keep PC prices rising into 2027
points.detail: Dell expects memory supply to stay tight in 2027, PCBs stay short until mid-2028, and European notebook revenue rose 16% on pricier models. We should plan inventory, pricing and mix for higher costs.

points.headline: AI PC demand is now the growth driver as the Windows 11 refresh fades
points.detail: HP says local-AI demand is lifting AI PC shipments past expectations, and Best Buy computing sales hold on gaming and AI demand. We should lead our store merchandising with AI-capable PCs.

points.headline: AI agents are becoming a deal-discovery and checkout channel
points.detail: Walmart put Black Friday deals into Meta's Muse agent, ChatGPT Wallet enables agent purchases, and NRF finds half of holiday shoppers plan to use AI. Our catalog and promos must be readable by agents.

points.headline: Amex projects a 14-year high in small business holiday spending
points.detail: Strong small-business budgets give our store a window to push business bundles, financing and bulk offers.
